given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)

breaks.break: Loan due today is treated as overdue (`<=`)
breaks.caught by: src/reminders/reminders.service.test.ts:70-77 (B2's loan-3 is due on the run day and must not be sent)

breaks.break: Loan that is not yet overdue is treated as overdue
'Today' is taken in local time rather than UTC

given.why: The test clock hands in a plain date string, so nothing here would fail if the code read 'today' in local time instead of UTC.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today

breaks.break: A reminder recorded on an earlier day blocks today's send
A loan with no reminder at all is skipped

given.why: No test seeds a reminder from a previous day and expects a send, so code that skips any loan with a past reminder would pass.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member

breaks.break: Never calls the API
Sends the wrong member, such as the loan id
Sends the wrong dueOn or loanId
Sends only one of the two overdue loans

then.why: The fake records each reminder, and the two loans have distinct members and ids, so each field is pinned.

then.part: then records a reminder for today

breaks.break: Nothing is recorded
Records the dueOn date instead of today
Records it before asking the API
breaks.caught by: src/reminders/reminders.service.test.ts:108-110 (B3 shows the refused loan is not recorded)

then.why: The recorded row and its date are checked here; the ask-before-record ordering is proved by B3, which asserts nothing is recorded on refusal.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today

breaks.break: Reminded loans are sent again on a second run

given.why: Running the job twice and expecting exactly one send fails if the dedupe is wrong.

breaks.break: Returned loans are still reminded
breaks.caught by: src/reminders/reminders.service.test.ts:72,77 (loan 2 is overdue and returned, and is absent from sent)

given.why: Loan 2 is overdue and returned, so only the returned filter excludes it.

breaks.break: A loan due today is reminded

given.why: Loan 3 sits on the boundary, so `<=` would send it and fail the assertion.

breaks.break: Any of the three excluded cases is sent
breaks.caught by: src/reminders/reminders.service.test.ts:77 (the sent list must be exactly loan 1)

breaks.break: Loan 1 is sent twice

then.why: toMatchObject against a one-element array pins both which loans were sent and how many times.

given.part: The Notifications API refuses or can't be reached

breaks.break: A refusal is treated as accepted
An unreachable API (a different reason string) is handled differently from a refusal

given.why: Only a refusal ('answered 503') is simulated at service level, and the unreachable reason is never fed through the job.

breaks.break: Records the reminder for the refused loan

then.why: The reminders table must equal exactly loan 2's row.

breaks.break: Wrong event name
Wrong level
Wrong loanId, such as the member id
Hard-coded or wrong error text

then.why: toContainEqual matches level, event and exact fields against the fake's reason.

then.part: carries on with the other loans

breaks.break: Stops at the first refusal

then.why: The refused loan is the earlier one, so a break that stops the run would leave loan 2 unsent.

Wrong level
sent count missing or wrong
failed count missing or wrong
sent and failed swapped

then.why: toEqual on the last log entry pins the level, event and both counts, with distinct values.

breaks.break: The client sends nothing

given.why: The test calls the client directly with a reminder and asserts the request that arrives.

then.part: Sends `POST {NOTIFY_URL}/notifications` with JSON `{ memberId, template: "loan-overdue", data: { loanId, dueOn } }`

breaks.break: Wrong HTTP method
Wrong path
Wrong content-type
A body field is renamed or has the wrong value, or the wrong template is used

then.why: toEqual on the captured request pins the method, path, content-type and the full body.

breaks.break: Only 200 is accepted
Only 202 is accepted
Some 2xx statuses are refused

then.why: Three different 2xx statuses are accepted, which rules out an exact-status check.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status

breaks.break: Only 5xx is refused, so a 4xx is accepted
The reason does not name the status
A 5xx answer is accepted

then.why: Only a 400 is tested, so a 5xx or a 3xx being accepted would pass every test.

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable

breaks.break: A connection failure throws instead of returning refused
The reason does not say the API was unreachable

then.why: No test makes the connection fail, for example with HttpResponse.error(), so this path is never run.
